info.title: trek
info.description: Badger Trek: free, cross-platform, hash-certified database migrations for SQL Server, Azure SQL, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle and SQLite, with real up and down, named changes, environments, Entra ID and Always Encrypted. Formerly Badger.SqlMigrate.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: Badger Trek - hash-certified, plan-based database migrations with real up and down.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information

options.name: --project
options.description: Project directory containing trek.yaml and trek.plan. [default: .]

options.name: --env
options.description: Environment from trek.yaml (or TREK_ENV; default: defaultEnvironment).

options.name: --connection-string
options.description: Connect exactly as this connection string says (replaces the environment's server, sign-in and TLS settings).

options.name: --claim-environment
options.description: Allow a database recorded under another environment name (e.g. restored from prod) and record this one. [default: False]

options.name: --var
options.description: Script variable, name=value. Repeatable.

options.name: --json
options.description: Machine-readable output on stdout. [default: False]

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Show server messages and details. [default: False]

options.name: --no-color
options.description: Disable ANSI colors (also honors NO_COLOR). [default: False]

options.name: --bundle
options.description: Run from a verified bundle (trek bundle create) instead of the project folder's scripts.

commands.name: init
commands.description: Create trek.yaml, trek.plan, folders and AGENTS.md in the project directory.

options.name: --provider
options.description: Database provider: sqlserver, postgresql, mysql, mariadb, oracle or sqlite. [default: sqlserver]

options.name: --no-agents-file
options.description: Do not write AGENTS.md (instructions for AI assistants) into the project. [default: False]

commands.name: add
commands.description: Add a change: creates changes/<name>/ scripts and appends it to trek.plan.

options.name: --requires
options.description: Changes this one depends on.

options.name: --note
options.description: Note stored in the plan.

options.name: --notx
options.description: Run outside a transaction. [default: False]

options.name: --irreversible
options.description: No revert script. [default: False]

options.name: --from-diff
options.description: Generate deploy.sql and revert.sql from schema edits made in the environment's database (compared with a shadow database built from the plan). [default: False]

options.name: --shadow-env
options.description: Create the shadow database on this environment's server instead (it needs CREATE DATABASE rights).

options.name: --keep-shadow
options.description: Do not drop the shadow database afterwards. [default: False]

options.name: --exclude
options.description: Objects to leave out, as schema.name globs (e.g. audit.*). Repeatable.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: With --from-diff: print the generated deploy script; write nothing. [default: False]

options.name: --no-record
options.description: With --from-diff: do not record the new change as applied in the database it came from. [default: False]

options.name: --author
options.description: Author written into trek.plan (default: TREK_AUTHOR, else git's user.name, else the OS user name).

commands.name: tag
commands.description: Tag the last change in the plan (use as @name in --to).

commands.name: plan
commands.description: Plan file commands.

commands.name: check
commands.description: Validate the plan, folders and scripts (no database needed). Use in CI and pre-commit hooks.

commands.name: show
commands.description: List planned changes with script hashes and chain ids (no database needed).

commands.name: status
commands.description: Compare the plan with the database.

options.name: --exit-code
options.description: Exit with 3 when the database is not up to date. [default: False]

commands.name: deploy
commands.description: Provision environment resources (Always Encrypted keys), then deploy pending changes and repeatables. The database must already exist.

options.name: --to
options.description: Deploy up to and including this change or @tag.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Show what would run without changing anything. [default: False]

options.name: --script
options.description: Write a reviewable SQL script of pending changes to this file instead of deploying.

options.name: --ordering
options.description: Override the environment's ordering policy (dependency|strict).

options.name: --yes
options.description: Do not ask for confirmation (required in non-interactive runs against protected environments). [default: False]

commands.name: revert
commands.description: Revert changes using the revert scripts stored in the database at deploy time.

options.name: --to
options.description: Revert everything deployed after this change or @tag.

options.name: --last
options.description: Revert the last N deployed changes.

options.name: --all
options.description: Revert every deployed change. [default: False]

options.name: --repeatable
options.description: Restore a repeatable (e.g. views/vCustomer.sql) to its definition before the last apply. Repeatable.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Show what would run without changing anything. [default: False]

options.name: --yes
options.description: Do not ask for confirmation (required in non-interactive runs against protected environments). [default: False]

options.name: --allow-variable-drift
options.description: Revert even if the revert script renders differently than at deploy time. [default: False]

commands.name: rebase
commands.description: Revert to a change, then redeploy to head (handy while iterating on a change).

options.name: --to
options.description: Revert to this change or @tag, then deploy to the plan head.

options.name: --yes
options.description: Do not ask for confirmation (required in non-interactive runs against protected environments). [default: False]

options.name: --allow-variable-drift
options.description: Revert even if the revert script renders differently than at deploy time. [default: False]

commands.name: repair
commands.description: Accept edits to deployed changes (e.g. a fixed revert.sql) without running anything; re-certifies the journal.

options.name: --all
options.description: Repair every deployed change whose hash no longer matches. [default: False]

options.name: --reason
options.description: Why the scripts were edited; recorded in the log.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Show what would run without changing anything. [default: False]

options.name: --yes
options.description: Do not ask for confirmation (required in non-interactive runs against protected environments). [default: False]

arguments.name: CHANGES
arguments.description: Deployed changes whose edited scripts should be accepted.

commands.name: rework
commands.description: Add a change that supersedes a deployed one: copies its deploy script to edit, with a revert that restores it.

options.name: --as
options.description: Name of the new change (default: <change>-v2, -v3, ...).

options.name: --note
options.description: Note stored in the plan.

commands.name: bundle
commands.description: Package the project into a hash-verified file to deploy with --bundle.

commands.name: create
commands.description: Write a bundle of the plan, changes, repeatables, environment scripts and trek.yaml.

options.name: --output
options.description: Bundle file to write (default: trek-bundle-<plan head>.zip).

options.name: --no-config
options.description: Leave trek.yaml out; deploys then read it from --project. [default: False]

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Check every file in a bundle against its manifest hashes.

commands.name: diff-schema
commands.description: Show schema differences: live vs. last recorded (what drifted), or between two environments.

options.name: --against
options.description: Compare with this environment's live database (default: this database's schema as recorded after its last deploy).

options.name: --exit-code
options.description: Exit with 3 when the schemas differ. [default: False]

options.name: --script
options.description: With --against: write SQL that turns this database into that one, to this file.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Check deployed hashes against the working copy, run verify scripts, and detect schema drift.

commands.name: log
commands.description: Show the deploy/revert/failure history recorded in the database.

options.name: --limit
options.description: Number of events. [default: 50]

commands.name: import
commands.description: Convert another tool's migrations (Flyway, DbUp, Entity Framework Core, grate, Sqitch, SQL projects) into a new trek project (written to --project).

options.name: --no-agents-file
options.description: Do not write AGENTS.md (instructions for AI assistants) into the project. [default: False]

commands.name: flyway
commands.description: Import a Flyway project: V/U/R scripts, placeholders, script config and environments.

options.name: --config
options.description: flyway.conf or flyway.toml (default: found in the folder or its conf/ folder).

options.name: --location
options.description: Migration folder; overrides flyway.locations. Repeatable.

options.name: --provider
options.description: The database the project targets: sqlserver (default), postgresql, mysql, mariadb, oracle or sqlite. Sqitch projects for pg, oracle or sqlite default to that provider.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Show what would be written without writing anything. [default: False]

commands.name: dbup
commands.description: Import DbUp scripts: one change per script in DbUp's order; $variables$ become {variables} (values via --var).

options.name: --file-names
options.description: DbUp script names are file names only (WithScriptsFromFileSystem); default: folder.path.names like embedded resources. [default: False]

options.name: --run-always
options.description: Glob of scripts DbUp runs every time (imported as repeatables). Repeatable.

options.name: --no-variables
options.description: The project disabled DbUp variables: leave $name$ text alone. [default: False]

options.name: --provider
options.description: The database the project targets: sqlserver (default), postgresql, mysql, mariadb, oracle or sqlite. Sqitch projects for pg, oracle or sqlite default to that provider.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Show what would be written without writing anything. [default: False]

commands.name: ef
commands.description: Import Entity Framework Core migrations: one change per migration, from Up() and Down() as SQL (dotnet ef migrations script). The provider comes from the SQL.

options.name: --down
options.description: With a script file: the down script, from 'dotnet ef migrations script <last migration> 0'. Without it, changes are !irreversible.

options.name: --context
options.description: The DbContext, when the project has several (passed to dotnet ef).

options.name: --startup-project
options.description: The project that configures the DbContext, when it is not the migrations project (passed to dotnet ef).

options.name: --provider
options.description: The database the project targets: sqlserver (default), postgresql, mysql, mariadb, oracle or sqlite. Sqitch projects for pg, oracle or sqlite default to that provider.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Show what would be written without writing anything. [default: False]

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: The project holding the migrations (trek runs 'dotnet ef' to script them), or a script from 'dotnet ef migrations script'.

commands.name: grate
commands.description: Import a grate or RoundhousE scripts folder: up/ as changes, anytime and everytime folders as repeatables, *.ENV.* scripts, {{Tokens}} (values via --var).

options.name: --folder
options.description: A renamed grate folder, key=name (e.g. up=ddl). Repeatable.

options.name: --environment
options.description: Environment names used in *.ENV.* file names (default: the upper-case parts of those names). Repeatable or comma-separated.

options.name: --ignore-directory-names
options.description: grate ran with --ignoredirectorynames: script names are file names only. [default: False]

options.name: --no-tokens
options.description: grate ran with --disabletokenreplacement: leave {{Token}} text alone. [default: False]

options.name: --provider
options.description: The database the project targets: sqlserver (default), postgresql, mysql, mariadb, oracle or sqlite. Sqitch projects for pg, oracle or sqlite default to that provider.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Show what would be written without writing anything. [default: False]

commands.name: sqitch
commands.description: Import a Sqitch project: plan order, dependencies, tags, reworks and deploy/revert/verify scripts.

options.name: --engine
options.description: Which engine's settings to use from sqitch.conf (default: core.engine).

options.name: --provider
options.description: The database the project targets: sqlserver (default), postgresql, mysql, mariadb, oracle or sqlite. Sqitch projects for pg, oracle or sqlite default to that provider.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Show what would be written without writing anything. [default: False]

commands.name: sqlproj
commands.description: Import an SSDT / SQL Database Project (.sqlproj): one change per table, type, schema ... in dependency order; views, procedures, functions and triggers as repeatables; the post-deployment script; SqlCmdVariables.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Show what would be written without writing anything. [default: False]

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: The .sqlproj file, or the folder holding it.

commands.name: convert
commands.description: Convert a live database between SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle and SQLite: its schema into a new trek project for the provider you choose (convert schema --to), then its rows (convert data).

options.name: --no-agents-file
options.description: Do not write AGENTS.md (instructions for AI assistants) into the project. [default: False]

commands.name: schema
commands.description: Read the source database's catalog and write a new project for the --to provider: changes for schemas, types, sequences, tables, keys and indexes; views, routines and triggers translated as repeatables; CONVERSION.md listing what to review.

options.name: --out
options.description: Folder for the new project (must not contain one yet).

options.name: --to
options.description: Target provider: sqlserver, postgresql, mysql, mariadb, oracle or sqlite.

options.name: --from-provider
options.description: The source provider when the source is a --connection-string rather than an environment of the project in --project.

options.name: --names
options.description: Identifiers in the target: lower (default for PostgreSQL), upper (default for Oracle), snake (CustomerOrder -> customer_order; CUSTOMER_ORDER on Oracle) or keep (default for SQL Server, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite).

options.name: --case-sensitive
options.description: Do not give PostgreSQL text columns a case-insensitive collation when the SQL Server database compares text case-insensitively. [default: False]

options.name: --exclude
options.description: schema.name glob of objects to leave out (* and ?). Repeatable.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Show what would be written without writing anything. [default: False]

commands.name: data
commands.description: Copy every table's rows from the source database into the converted, deployed target: parents first, identities and sequences moved past the copied values, row counts compared.

options.name: --target
options.description: The project 'convert schema' wrote (already deployed).

options.name: --target-env
options.description: Environment of the target project to load into (default: its defaultEnvironment).

options.name: --from-provider
options.description: The source provider when the source is a --connection-string rather than an environment of the project in --project.

options.name: --tables
options.description: schema.name glob of source tables to copy (* and ?). Repeatable; default all.

options.name: --truncate
options.description: Empty the target tables first (otherwise they must be empty). [default: False]

commands.name: baseline
commands.description: Adopt an existing database: record changes as applied without running them.

options.name: --to
options.description: Mark changes up to this one as already applied (with --from sqlproj: further than the imported changes).

options.name: --from
options.description: flyway | dbup | ef | grate | roundhouse | sqitch: read what the database already has from that tool's journal; sqlproj: the database was published from the SQL project (for projects made with 'trek import').

options.name: --journal
options.description: The tool's journal table, [schema.]table (default: flyway_schema_history, SchemaVersions or __EFMigrationsHistory in dbo/public/main, grate.ScriptsRun, RoundhousE.ScriptsRun, sqitch.changes; on Oracle, in the environment's schema: SCHEMAVERSIONS for DbUp, GRATE_SCRIPTSRUN for grate (SCHEMA_SCRIPTSRUN with grate --schema), CHANGES for Sqitch (REGISTRY.CHANGES when Sqitch used another registry); RoundhousE needs --journal).

options.name: --skip-checksums
options.description: Do not compare Flyway's checksums, grate's hashes or Sqitch's script hashes with the imported scripts (sqlproj: do not check that the project's tables exist). [default: False]

options.name: --yes
options.description: Do not ask for confirmation (required in non-interactive runs against protected environments). [default: False]

commands.name: vars
commands.description: List built-in and user variables for an environment, resolved ({name} and $(name) in scripts).

commands.name: render
commands.description: Print a script exactly as it would be sent to the database for an environment.

options.name: --kind
options.description: deploy | revert | verify (changes only). [default: deploy]

commands.name: env
commands.description: Environment commands.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List environments (templates start with '_').

commands.name: show
commands.description: Show the fully resolved environment (extends merged, secrets masked).

commands.name: status
commands.description: Compare per-environment resources (e.g. Always Encrypted keys) with the database.

commands.name: provision
commands.description: Create or rotate per-environment resources without deploying changes.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Show what would run without changing anything. [default: False]

options.name: --allow-destructive
options.description: Also apply destructive steps, e.g. drop a column encryption key value protected by a retired master key. [default: False]

options.name: --yes
options.description: Do not ask for confirmation (required in non-interactive runs against protected environments). [default: False]

commands.name: auth
commands.description: Entra ID sign-in commands.

commands.name: clear
commands.description: Forget saved interactive/device-code sign-ins so the next run signs in again.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Check configuration, sign-in and connectivity for an environment and explain problems.

commands.name: ai-guide
commands.description: Print the guide for AI assistants writing changes in a trek project (Markdown).

commands.name: mcp
commands.description: Run a Model Context Protocol server over stdio for AI assistants: tools that read and write this project's files. It never connects to a database.
